content.text:
I can build the sponsor pitch deck, but three things you listed have been retired or aren't accurate, so I'm adjusting them rather than including them as asked:

- **"Companies sponsor, people activate, impact is delivered" as a model**: this three-sided framing was retired. Sponsors are one funding type, not a separate structural pillar. The current model is Activate (dominant) + Fund (secondary), with sponsoring organizations creating funded capacity for their people, attributed subtly ("Made possible by [Sponsor]").
- **501(c)(3) approval**: ActivateGratitude.org's determination is unconfirmed. I can't state it as granted anywhere, including a sponsor deck. I'll mark it [NEEDS INPUT] and keep any tax-deductibility language out.
- **$1M founder commitment**: this has been removed from all messaging. I'm leaving it out entirely.

Here's the deck built the right way, positioning sponsorship as funded capacity within the real Activate + Fund model:

```json
[
  {"type": "title", "title": "Gratitude, delivered.", "subtitle": "Sponsor Kit: Fund capacity your people can activate", "notes": "Open with the category line and the sponsor value prop in one breath."},
  {"type": "content", "title": "The problem", "body": "People care. Organizations care. The missing piece is infrastructure.", "bullets": ["Good intention is common. A shared way to act on it is not.", "Most corporate giving ends with a receipt, not a result.", "Employees and customers want to participate, not just watch a company give."], "notes": "Set up why sponsorship through Gratitude is different from a CSR check."},
  {"type": "content", "title": "How Gratitude.com works", "body": "Real acts of good are funded first, so a person can put one into motion instantly.", "bullets": ["Pre-fund: capacity is committed before anyone clicks", "Activate: a person chooses an available act, at no cost to them, in the moment", "Deliver: a trusted nonprofit partner carries it out", "Verify: delivery is confirmed, not assumed", "Show Impact: the participant, and the funder, see what happened"], "notes": "This is the full mechanism. Keep Activate and Fund clearly distinct throughout the deck."},
  {"type": "two-column", "title": "Two ways in, always distinct", "left": {"heading": "Activate", "bullets": ["The dominant action", "Choose an available pre-funded act", "Costs the participant nothing"]}, "right": {"heading": "Fund", "bullets": ["The secondary action", "Creates capacity for future acts", "One-time or recurring", "This is where sponsorship lives"]}, "notes": "Sponsorship is a form of Fund, not a third pillar. Keep this distinction sharp for the sponsor audience."},
  {"type": "content", "title": "Where your organization fits", "body": "Sponsoring organizations create funded capacity for their employees, customers, or communities to activate.", "bullets": ["You fund real acts in advance", "Your people choose one and activate it", "A trusted nonprofit partner delivers it", "Attribution stays subtle: \"Made possible by [Sponsor]\"", "Your brand never overpowers the act or the participant's choice"], "notes": "This replaces the retired three-sided sponsor model. Sponsorship funds capacity inside the same Activate + Fund system everyone else uses."},
  {"type": "content", "title": "What your people see", "body": "Not a donation ask. A moment of agency.", "bullets": ["An available act, already funded and ready", "One clear choice: activate it", "A verified result they can follow", "\"Your good landed.\""], "notes": "Emphasize this doesn't feel like a charity marketplace or a corporate giving campaign."},
  {"type": "content", "title": "What you see as a funder", "body": "Funders get a result loop too.", "bullets": ["What your funded capacity made possible", "Verified delivery, not a pledge total", "Participation from your own people, not a generic report", "Most giving ends with a receipt. Gratitude ends with a result."], "notes": "This is the sponsor's ROI moment. Keep it concrete and non-hyped."},
  {"type": "stats", "title": "The opportunity", "stats": [{"value": "$100B+", "label": "Corporate wellbeing and engagement spend, 2026"}, {"value": "$240B", "label": "Projected by 2035"}, {"value": "82%", "label": "Of employees say recognition matters"}, {"value": "[NEEDS INPUT]", "label": "Verified activations to date"}], "notes": "Market stats are sourced from loaded research. Traction numbers are not yet approved for external use and are marked accordingly."},
  {"type": "content", "title": "The entities behind it", "body": "Two organizations, two jobs.", "bullets": ["Gratitude.com, Inc.: a Delaware C-Corp, B Corp pending. Makes participation possible.", "ActivateGratitude.org: the charitable entity. Makes the impact possible.", "501(c)(3) determination for ActivateGratitude.org: [NEEDS INPUT], not yet confirmed", "Tax treatment of any funding: to be confirmed, not stated as deductible"], "notes": "This is the accurate entity slide. Do not state 501(c)(3) as granted or imply tax deductibility until legal confirms."},
  {"type": "content", "title": "What's next for participation", "body": "Sponsorship funds what's available now, with more ways in coming.", "bullets": ["NOW: Activate and Fund, fully live", "NEXT: Express, acknowledging someone directly", "FUTURE: Facilitate, helping deliver the act itself"], "notes": "Keep sponsors oriented to NOW. Don't sell Express or Facilitate as available today."},
  {"type": "closing", "title": "Fund the next act", "subtitle": "gratitude.com", "body": "Create funded capacity for your people, and see what it makes possible.", "notes": "Close on Fund as the sponsor's action, tied back to a real result."}
]
```

This gives you a sponsor deck that's accurate and still makes a strong case: sponsorship as funded capacity inside a system your people actually participate in, not a logo slapped on a donation drive. The market and problem stats are ones already verified in the brand kit; the two traction and entity-status placeholders need real numbers or legal sign-off before this goes external.

Want me to also draft the sponsor pricing/tiers section once you have those numbers, or generate a cover image for the deck?
